title: fix(workboard): recover after database connection loss
body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a PostgreSQL connection is lost, Workboard can keep using the closed connection and fail subsequent requests.

## User Impact

The existing worker recovery path can reopen the store on the next request. Failed requests are not replayed. No schema, schema-version, stored-format, retention, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard catches operation errors and returns a structured failure. That reply alone does not retire an unusable connection. The native kernel now checks settlement, and the worker forwards that check through the existing hook. Error results and close behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `f0389e586225150b3d75d327b83e9035be68ddff`; base: `6f8c9bad8bd1a8c339f2d61985e637f9e557550d`.
- SQLite Workboard suite: 31 files, 362 tests passed; 12 PostgreSQL-only tests skipped.
- Focused PostgreSQL settlement/recovery run: 2 files, 4 tests passed. The real public-store test terminates only the fixture's blocked writer, verifies the failed write is absent, then reads and writes through the same facade without replay. Domain errors are preserved before and after recovery.
- The preceding full PostgreSQL Workboard suite passed 338 tests at `9dcfd05831bb74d7465862d77564509ec567a428`. Production and PostgreSQL-test bytes are unchanged; the final amendment fixes mixed sync/async test cleanup flagged by lint.
- Final-head test typecheck and targeted lint passed with zero warnings/errors. Production typecheck, format, database-worker/dialect ratchets, lifecycle-owner tests and import-cycle checks also passed.
- Fresh exact-head independent P2 review: no findings.
- Proof: [Blacksmith Testbox run 41676457364](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41676457364). Completed Testbox commands exited 0 before the lease reached its one-hour workflow limit. The later cancelled workflow status does not represent an interrupted test command.
- Production: +13/-0 lines. Tests: +242/-0 lines.

The broad changed-check run reported seven unused-export findings outside this diff. The exact unchanged base reproduces the same seven entries across the production and full-tree Knip scans; they are existing repository debt, not introduced by this repair. The Knip check remains red. This test does not cover an ambiguous COMMIT outcome.


## Regression replay

The unchanged public termination/recovery regression failed on the unpatched frozen base with `PostgreSQL connection lost; transaction rolled back` on the next request. The interrupted request had already been observed as rejected. The same public flow passes at this PR head. Replayed with test-only overlays and unchanged production on the recorded base through Blacksmith Testbox.

## Landing refresh — 2026-11-04

Current head: `05c3115c9745bc5f8fe3edd31e0d8496e68e01bd`. Integrated frozen main `d27139b2b220327d6f65b659c6fba0b0110fad97`; independent integration review found no new source defect. Earlier exact-head evidence above remains explicitly attributed and is reused only for unchanged inputs. Maintainer landing is now authorized; GitHub checks and native landing guards remain enforced.

Combined Track A candidate tree `6059134c361ed8602271261ddb940c9b9d1b413e`: **1,183 tests passed, 12 intentional skips** across tooling, sessions, plugin workers and Matrix. The repository transaction-boundary guard passed. Test-line total and ceiling both equal **6,447,876**; allocations credit only each change’s literal added test lines. Real PostgreSQL integration recheck is in progress and is not counted as passed here.

No DDL, schema-version/fingerprint, persisted representation, retention/durability, identity, or recovery-authority changes are introduced by this PR. This is scoped functional proof, not a global PostgreSQL or performance qualification.

Current merged-base CI has an inherited test-line ceiling deficit: main toast commit `1be3b6d2a1a786a325724faf9126010b7195087f` added 46 test lines without credit (+44 in `ui/src/lib/toast.browser.test.ts`, +2 in `ui/src/e2e/chat-attachment-toast.test-support.ts`). This PR’s own added lines are fully allocated. Exact failed-run attribution remains a separate native landing requirement.

## Completed integration qualification

Targeted real PostgreSQL qualification completed: **50 tests passed across 13 files**, including the five newly registered inventory suites, public recovery paths and session-bound/cold-selection regressions. Schema parity checks found zero unexplained differences. The real cold maintenance workload also passed its0/0 full-batch scan and2/2 mixed-batch scan expectations, with admission checks retained.

Seven relevant type configurations and four scoped lint groups completed without diagnostics. The one README separator-format failure was corrected and the repository formatter check passed. Runtime tests remain tied to tree `6059134c361ed8602271261ddb940c9b9d1b413e`; tree `338bef659fad31f557af06c4930cf4ce6a628733` differs only by that Markdown blank line.

The remaining test-line red is attributed to unchanged main toast inputs; this PR’s exact failed run and two-parent merge are recorded in native landing evidence. That red is not called a passing check.
